title: Nordic frequency event · Kvilldal trip
description: A winter weekday morning at the Elhub reference peak hour (2026-01-12 08:00): Norway serves about 24 GW and exports about 2.2 GW net over its interconnectors, and the rest of the Nordic synchronous area runs at winter-peak kinetic energy. A few 132 kV lines already run above their ratings and hold overload alarms. Two minutes in, Kvilldal (Suldal, NO2), Norway's largest hydropower station, trips while generating about 1,080 MW. The rest of the Nordic area takes part as a synchronous equivalent with its own inertia and reserves behind the real ties to Sweden and Finland. Inertia limits the rate of fall, FCR-N and FCR-D arrest it well above the 48.8 Hz first stage of under-frequency load shedding, and aFRR and then mFRR bring the frequency back to 50 Hz within about twenty minutes. Branch flows and bus voltages come from an AC load flow of the energised island. Nothing else changes the grid: there are no weather-driven faults.
objectives: Before the trip, read the island frequency, the dispatch of the largest units and the allocated FCR-N, FCR-D, aFRR and mFRR volumes (grid.summary, islands.list).

When Kvilldal trips, follow the nadir, the rate of change of frequency and the FCR-D activation that arrests the fall; confirm that no under-frequency load-shedding stage operates and no other unit trips.

Follow the restoration: FCR holds the frequency below 50 Hz after the arrest, aFRR starts to restore it, and mFRR, activated once aFRR has been used persistently, brings it back into the ±100 mHz standard range and to 50 Hz and releases the activated FCR.

Assess what is left for a second incident: compare the activated FCR, aFRR and mFRR of the largest units (asset.get) with their allocated volumes, and propose the re-dispatch or unit starts that would restore the reserves before the next trip.

cues.title: Read the baseline before the scheduled trip

guidance.title: Winter peak before a unit trip
guidance.message: Use Guide or inspect the starting frequency, allocated reserves and generator state directly. The model schedules a Kvilldal trip at +2 min. Shared time starts paused until a person advances or plays it.

guidance.title: Inspect the generator-trip response
guidance.message: Inspect the actual Kvilldal state and cue outcome. Follow measured nadir and FCR-D, then aFRR and mFRR in the model. Check recovery, observation time and reserves remaining; the scheduled event does not establish that frequency reached 50 Hz.

guide.title: Follow a frequency event
guide.description: An illustrative Nordic-grid reserve exercise. Observe actual frequency and reserves rather than taking the scripted prose as evidence.

steps.title: Read the baseline
steps.instruction: Open Grid operations. Inspect current frequency, reserves and the Kvilldal generator before the event.

steps.title: Advance to two minutes
steps.instruction: Advance the shared Run to the two-minute generator trip. Check the cue journal and the actual generator state.

steps.title: Follow the arrest
steps.instruction: Advance in bounded intervals and inspect the frequency trend and FCR-D response. A browser highlight cannot establish a nadir; use the recorded series and its time range.

steps.title: Observe recovery
steps.instruction: Continue in bounded intervals while reading aFRR, mFRR and residual reserves. This gate checks a fresh largest-load-island frequency of at least 49.9 Hz; it does not establish that every island or all reserves recovered.

steps.title: Explain the evidence
steps.instruction: State what the model showed, which island the frequency represents, when each reserve responded and what capacity remains. Treat this as an illustrative model result, not validation of the real Nordic grid.

steps.title: Continue exploring
steps.instruction: This guide is finished. The same Run remains available. Pause or stop guidance whenever you wish; those controls do not pause the shared simulation. Copy the Run before trying a different intervention. Acknowledgements record your choice to continue, not a qualification.
